variants.title: Balmer lines with a 300 lines/mm grating
variants.sample: Hydrogen discharge tube, 300 lines/mm replica grating
variants.note: A coarse grating throws the lines out at smaller angles, so all four Balmer lines are easy to find - but each angle is read less accurately.

source.title: Standard laboratory replica transmission gratings: 300, 600 and 1200 rulings per millimetre

variants.title: Balmer lines with a 1200 lines/mm grating
variants.sample: Hydrogen discharge tube, 1200 lines/mm replica grating
variants.note: A fine grating spreads the spectrum much further, so the angles are large and the reading is more accurate. Beyond sin θ = 1 a line is not diffracted at all, which sets the limit on how fine a grating may be used.

source.title: Standard laboratory replica transmission gratings: 300, 600 and 1200 rulings per millimetre

variants.title: Balmer lines in the second order
variants.sample: Hydrogen discharge tube, 600 lines/mm grating, second order
variants.note: The same grating in its second order throws each line out to roughly twice the angle, so the same vernier reads the wavelength more precisely. The second order is fainter, and the faintest Balmer line may be hard to see.

source.title: Standard laboratory replica transmission gratings: 300, 600 and 1200 rulings per millimetre
